# Thumbnails are generated by the API on upload with SkiaSharp

Phase 2 adds a Thumbnail for every Image so listings stop downloading full-size pictures. The API generates it right after validating an upload: at most 480 px wide (never upscaled), encoded as WebP at quality 80, stored next to the original with the same image storage (`{tenantId}/{productId}/{imageId}-thumb.webp`). The original is kept unchanged for the product page. Image processing uses SkiaSharp (MIT licensed) with the `SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux.NoDependencies` package so the API container needs no extra system libraries.

## Considered Options

- **ImageSharp**: simplest API, rejected because its license is not free for every commercial use.
- **Resizing at the edge (Cloudflare Images or image transformations)**: no code to write, rejected because it is not free and ties the demo to a paid feature.
- **Resizing in the browser before upload**: rejected because the API cannot trust what it receives and old clients would skip it.

## Consequences

- Images uploaded before this change have no Thumbnail; responses fall back to the original URL.
- Deleting an Image deletes its Thumbnail too; duplicating a product copies both.
- Upload latency grows by the resize time; acceptable at 2 MB per image.
